key_insight: Photon-drag photocurrents in altermagnets split into symmetry-specific angular harmonics that encode the Néel domain, enabling all-optical magnetic readout from polarized light measurements.
engineering_relevance: This offers a symmetry-based, noncontact way to detect and distinguish magnetic domains in device materials relevant to optoelectronics and next-generation spintronic/solar-energy platforms.
method: Analyze second-order photon-drag currents versus sample rotation angle.
Compare linear and circular polarization channels to separate domain-even and domain-odd terms.
Use harmonic selection rules and mirror symmetries to identify magnetic order ($d_{x^2-y^2}$, $d_{xy}$, and $g$-wave).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports symmetry-resolved theoretical analysis showing that 90°-rotated measurements on a single domain isolate domain-odd currents, with distinct harmonic signatures depending on polarization and magnetic order.
watch_item: The domain-odd charge-current signal requires spin-orbit coupling, so materials with weak SOC may be difficult to read out experimentally.
paper_title: Reading Altermagnetic Domains with Photon Drag
